newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end flat to lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended flat to down 1/4 point, while in new issues underwriters raised yields on several new deals.
"It seems like (there are) a fair amount of bonds in the market, not as much going away as one might hope," one trader said.
PaineWebber Inc reported a $28 million balance on a $65 million deal by Jordan School District, Utah, a triple-A rated issuer.

The trader said that while bankers may have advised issuers to take advantage of July 1 redemption money, Standard & Poor's Blue List is at close to $1.5 billion. That level is "as high as it's been recently," he said. Retail demand has also been "relatively slow," the trader said.
"(The market) is sort of very quietly backing up," he said.
A municipal analyst said dollar bonds closed down 1/8 to 1/4 point, while high-grade issues finished unchanged but "wobbly." Secondary activity was light to moderate, he said.

In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed up 4/32 at 117-12/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 12/32 at 111-25/32. The MOB spread was 179 ticks. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 4/32 at 99-3/32 to yield 6.69 percent near the close of New York trading.

On the economic front, the Conference Board Tuesday said U.S. consumer confidence in June hit its highest level since August 1969. Consumer confidence rose to 129.6 in June versus a revised 127.9 in May. A Reuters survey of economists reflected expectations for a 126.3 June reading.
Wednesday's economic news includes May durable goods. Economists polled Reuters expect a 0.6 percent rise.

Turning to new issues, PaineWebber Inc repriced Atlanta's $268 million water and sewer bond deal, raising yields in several maturities and lifting the top yield in 2027 to 5.55 percent from 5.526 percent.
Smith Barney Inc also repriced Tampa Sports Authority's $150 million bond offering, raising yields in several maturities. The top yield was raised to 5.56 percent from 5.535 in 2027.
Commonwealth Securities and Investments Inc tentatively priced $180 million Allegheny County Sanitary Authority, Pa., sewer revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.63 percent in 2024.
An analyst said some of the new negotiated deals came at aggressive levels initially, but reflected more realistic levels once they were repriced.
On the competitive side, Merrill Lynch & Co won $300 million Massachusetts general obligation bonds at a true cost of 5.19 percent.
Key Capital Markets won $100 million Gwinnett County Water and Sewerage Authority, Ga., revenue bonds at a net interest cost of 5.25 percent.
Looking ahead to Wednesday, municipal bond sales are expected to total $4 billion in 35 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $3.6 billion in 20 sales, with a $2.8 billion New Jersey Economic Development Authority deal through Merrill Lynch topping the list.
